title: Burst Credit Allocator & Quarantine Lanes — PRD (draft)
body:
Summary:

This is an exploratory PRD for a feature set that manages temporary burst capacity for Dedicated tenants while protecting cluster-level SLOs and tenant isolation. The core idea is a credit-based burst allocator plus a quarantine lane mechanism that isolates noisy tenants when they exceed safe thresholds. The goal is to give tenants more headroom for short spikes without jeopardizing other customers or requiring manual ops intervention.

Why we need this now:
- Increasing number of Dedicated customers asking for predictable short-term burst beyond reserved reservations.
- Manual burst approvals and ad-hoc failovers create ops load and poor customer experience.
- Need a single, auditable mechanism that ties burst eligibility to historical behavior, SLOs, and current cluster health.

Goals (measurable):
- Support ephemeral bursts up to 3x baseline for up to 10 minutes for eligible tenants.
- Limit cross-tenant p99 latency regressions to <5% when bursts occur.
- Reduce manual burst-related support tickets by 70% in first 6 months.
- Expose per-tenant burst accounting for billing/chargeback.

Non-goals:
- This PRD does not cover long-term capacity resizing (reserved capacity changes).
- Not implementing a new billing product — only exportable usage records for billing.

Primary user stories:
- As a platform admin, I want automated safeguards that prevent a tenant burst from impacting other tenants' latency SLOs.
- As a tenant, I want short burst windows so production traffic spikes don’t cause throttling or errors.
- As a CS rep, I want visibility into a tenant's burst consumption and ability to temporarily quarantine a tenant if they consistently violate patterns.

High-level approach (concepts):
1) Burst Credit Allocator (BCA): each tenant has a credit balance derived from reservation, historical variance, and contractual headroom. Credits are consumed when a tenant exceeds baseline throughput. Credits recharge at a configurable rate.

2) Quarantine Lanes: when a tenant's behavior (credit depletion, repeated violations, or severe noise) threatens cluster SLOs, we move them into a quarantined execution lane. Quarantine reduces priority, limits burst ceilings, and optionally redirects to a lower-cost model variant (soft-degradation). Quarantine is temporary and should have automated release conditions.

3) Predictive Admission Controller: uses short-term workload signals (queue depth, token production rate, recent p99 latency delta) and model of cluster headroom to approve or deny burst admission.

4) Accounting & Visibility: every burst decision emits an event (tenant, delta, justification, post-condition). We persist records for billing export and CS review.

Component breakdown:
- Controller service (new): evaluates burst requests, maintains credits, enforces quarantine. Exposes GRPC/HTTP API consumed by serving runtime and Console.
- Runtime hooks (serving runtime): queries controller at request admission and tags requests as burst or baseline. Needs to support preemptible work and priority lanes.
- Console UI: burst dashboard per tenant (current credits, last bursts, quarantine history) and operator controls (manual quarantine, forgiveness, credit top-up).
- Telemetry pipeline: new metrics (burst_attempts, burst_granted, burst_denied_reasons, credits_remaining, quarantine_events) + traces.

APIs (sketch):
- POST /v1/tenant/{id}/burst-check {requested_delta, window_s} -> {allow: bool, used_credits: int, reason: string}
- GET /v1/tenant/{id}/credits -> {balance, regen_rate, last_updated}
- POST /v1/admin/tenant/{id}/quarantine {action: enter|release, reason, until?} -> {ok}
(These are placeholders — runtime will need an efficient low-latency path.)

Console UX (notes):
- Tenant page: small graph of credits over time, list of recent bursts with contextual metrics (p50/p95/p99 pre/post).
- Operator page: queue of tenants currently restricted / quarantined with one-click release and audit trail.

SLO & safety constraints:
- Admission controller must be conservative while cluster headroom is < 15% (configurable).
- If cluster-level p99 latency increases beyond threshold, controller should immediately begin denying bursts and consider quarantining top offenders.
- We will support two quarantine modes: soft (priority lowered; fallback model variant) and hard (deny bursts, cap throughput). Hard mode requires manual override.

Billing/Accounting:
- Bursts consume a separate internal currency (credits). We'll export events for billing: {tenant, start_ts, end_ts, tokens_generated, credits_consumed, chargeable_units}.
- Need mapping from credits to dollar units for chargeback; product can decide on pricing separately.

Operational considerations:
- Backwards compatibility: default behavior for tenants with no allocation = deny bursts.
- Data retention: keep burst event log for 90 days for CS + 1 year for audits.
- Emergency kill-switch: global operator API to disable bursts cluster-wide.

Security & compliance:
- All admin actions must be logged with actor info.
- Quarantine decisions should be explainable in audit logs (signal + threshold hit).

Rollout strategy (phases):
- Phase 0: internal dogfooding on dedicated dev clusters; expose nothing to customers.
- Phase 1: Minimal tenant-facing feature: enable burst for a small set of customers with conservative limits and manual ops guardrails. Collect telemetry.
- Phase 2: Auto-allocator enabled for more tenants; expose Console controls.
- Phase 3: Open to all tenants with billing and SLA adjustments.

Metrics to monitor (initial):
- burst_granted_rate, burst_denied_rate, credits_consumed_per_tenant, quarantine_rate, cluster_p99_delta_post_burst, support_ticket_rate_related_to_burst

Open questions / trade-offs:
- Credit model: should credits be purely time-based (regen) or tied to historical variance and contractual weighting? (Hybrid probably best.)
- How aggressive should quarantine be by default? We can lean conservative at launch.
- Cost model: do we bill bursts at premium or consume existing committed capacity first? Product decision needed.
- API latency impact: adding an admission-check RPC in the request path risks added tail latency. Consider asynchronous approval for non-urgent requests or local fast-cache for credits.

Immediate next steps / TODOs:
- [ ] Align with Infra on admission RPC latency budget (SLA < 3ms ideally). (Owner: Liam)
- [ ] Prototype BCA state machine in a dev cluster (Owner: Ravi).
- [ ] Design Console mockups for credit dashboard (Owner: Marta).
- [ ] Draft billing mapping options and hand to pricing (Owner: Aisha).
- [ ] Create JIRA epic and link infra/serving/runtime tickets (blocked: decision on RPC path).

Notes to self / rough ideas:
- Consider using per-tenant local tokens in runtime to avoid round-trip check for every token generation (leaky bucket locally refilled by controller asynchronously).
- Quarantine lanes could be a generalized tenant-priority feature used for other operational policies (malicious traffic, compliance holds).

References / related docs:
- RFC: Dedicated Admission Controls (internal) — GHPR#2412
- Confluence notes (link above)

This is intentionally a working draft. I expect multiple iterations: the design must balance low-latency serving constraints with conservative cluster protection. We'll refine the credit math and quarantine heuristics after we have early telemetry from a small cohort.
